item.title: Taiwan President Pushes $6.6B Attack Drone Plan
item.description: Taiwan President Lai Ching-te reviewed domestic drone industrial efforts last week ahead of his administration’s push for a $6.6 billion attack drone plan to enhance the island’s defense against Chinese aggression. On Friday, Lai and members of the Taiwan Cabinet visited the National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology’s (NCSIST) Taichung facilities to review existing and ongoing unmanned programs. The state-run defense firm specializes in development of aircraft, missiles and long-range strike systems. Lai emphasized the need to domestically develop and produce drones to help counter Beijing’s increased “verbal and military intimidation” against Taiwan, according to the Presidential Communications Office.

item.title: Marist Brothers Old Pupils Association thanks all who helped make its local fundraising campaign a success
item.description:
By 
Samoa News staff
reporters@samoanews.com

Pago Pago, AMERICAN SAMOA — The Marist Brothers Old Pupils Association (MBOPA) extends its immense gratitude to our community, partners and sponsors following the successful conclusion of its American Samoa Fundraising Campaign.

According to a press release from MBOPA, it travelled to American Samoa in the beginning of July 2026 to commence its Fund-raising initiatives. “It was an amazing, successful and a memorable event for us,” the organization states.

It wishes to especially acknowledge the American Samoa community, family and friends for their love and support. 

“First and foremost, MBOPA gives thanks and glory to our Heavenly Father. His divine protection, guidance and blessings were fully upon us throughout our three-day Fundraising initiative in American Samoa, aimed at the critical renovation of the St Joseph’s College, Centennial Hall.”

MBOPA takes this opportunity to express their most heartfelt appreciation to everyone who offered their generous support. It notes that “this milestone initiative would not have been the phenomenal success it was without the active participation, selfless contributions and prayers of the community. Your involvement made these events truly memorable.”

Notably, special emphasis is placed “on the unwavering love and backing received from our sponsors” — TAULA Beverages, Lau Afioga Faumuina Enele Westerlund and SILVA Group, Afioga Sala Leslie Silva and Afioga Fainu’ulelei Jacinta Silva.

“We truly believe, without your invaluable sponsorship and the Good Lord’s blessings, this fundraising mission would not have been possible,” which began when the initial campaign launched in Pago Pago in April 2026, all the way through months of preparations of the grand finale,

The raffle draw was held on July 4, 2026, at the Bowling Alley, and “the overwhelming level of assistance we received far exceeded our expectations, serving as a powerful testament to your shared commitment to our goals.”

MBOPA continues that the financial support raised will directly fund the renovation of the Centennial Hall. This project is vital to improving school campus facilities and ensuring we can successfully cater to the educational and structural needs of the students and staff at our beloved St. Joseph’s College.

The group were also deeply honored by the presence of His Grace the Bishop Kolio Tumanuvao Etuale, the Governor of American Samoa, Pulaali’i Nikolao Pula and First Lady Dr. Lois Phillips Pula and Miss American Samoa Tilomai Tauiliili at the Corporate Table Dinner. “Your attendance added immense dignity to the occasion and made the evening truly special and memorable for everyone involved.”

MBOPA further noted that its fundraising success would not have been possible without the generosity of the business community in Pago, which included the Tool Shop, KS Mart, Western Union at Nu’uuli, Samoa Money Transfer at Pago Pago, Fagatogo Market, GIAS and McDonald’s Family Restaurant. Additionally, they thank Bluesky- American Samoa for providing  free SIM cards to MBOPA’s entire team during their time in American Samoa.

They also extend their gratitude to their partners in Upolu, Samoa, acknowledging the support of Samoa’s Prime Minister La'auli Leuatea Schmidt and everyone who donated ‘ie toga’ for the trip such as our Patrons and members of the Clergy.

“We highly appreciate SSAB and Tanoa for providing generous discounts on our MBOPA uniforms, which our team proudly wore during the Corporate Table event. Through our network of schools and houses, the Marist family generously contributed all the essential supplies for the trip.

“A special note of gratitude goes to Reverend Sasa Satoa and the Marist fraternity in Pago Pago. Your commitment to our Marist Spirit and hands-on assistance from the very beginning to the end of this Fundraising initiative were vital to our success.”

Thank you all for standing with us every step of the way, MBOPA concluded.

MBOPA says it is still receiving donations from the fundraiser and will finalize the financial report when done.

item.title: ASCC-ACNR celebrates grand opening of newly renovated Fale Samoa
item.description:
By 
Pauliana F Vitale, ACNR Media Specialist

Pago Pago, AMERICAN SAMOA — The American Samoa Community College (ASCC) Agriculture, Community and Natural Resources (ACNR) Division celebrated the opening of its newly renovated Fale Samoa on July 1, 2026  marking the completion of a project that will enhance community-focused research at the college.

The ceremony began with welcoming remarks from ACNR Director Aufaʻi Apulu Ropeti Areta, who greeted guests, staff, and community members gathered for the special occasion. An opening prayer was then offered by Pastor Autagavaia Alfred Peters, setting the tone for a celebration centered on gratitude and service.

As part of the program, outgoing ASCC President Dr. Rosevonne Pato was recognized as the guest of honor. In appreciation of her years of dedicated leadership and service to the College, Dr. Pato was invited to officially dedicate the new Fale Samoa by cutting the ceremonial ribbon.

Joining her was Vice President Dr. Letupu Moananu, attending on behalf of interim President Sonny J. Leomiti and the ASCC administration. Their participation reflected the College's support for the ACNR Division and the completion of the Fale Samoa.

Following the ribbon-cutting ceremony, guests took part in a traditional ʻava ceremony, commemorating the opening in accordance with Samoan custom. The event concluded with the presentation of fine mats to Dr. Pato as a heartfelt farewell gift, symbolizing the division’s appreciation and respect.

Gifts of fine mats were also presented to Vice President Moananu and interim President Leomiti and IEAD Executive Director Maʻauga Tauvela Fale in recognition of their continued support and their presence during the celebration.

Director Aufaʻi Areta thanked the U.S. Department of Agriculture's National Institute of Food and Agriculture for funding the project and acknowledged the support of the ASCC administration and campus offices that helped facilitate the project, as well as the contractor, VAA Construction, for bringing it to fruition. He noted that the new Fale Samoa will continue to serve as a welcoming space, supporting ACNR's research mission while preserving the traditions and heritage of American Samoa.

For more information on ACNR and its programs, visit their website at:  acnr.amsamoa.edu.

item.title: Fire in Ottoville last Friday displaces 14 members of one family
item.description:
By 
Samoa News staff
reporters@samoanews.com

Pago Pago, AMERICAN SAMOA — Another major fire occurred last Friday afternoon, July 17, 2026, this time in Ottoville — in a family compound.  According to witnesses who were on hand, helping to put out the fire, two (2) of the three homes that burned were gutted by fire, while the third home was partially burned. No one was injured.

It’s alleged that low water pressure, strong gusts of wind, and slow response from the Fire Department contributed to the fire spreading swiftly through the homes.

Fourteen people are reported to be displaced, of which 8 are children. The 6 adults include an 88-year-old elderly grandmother, whose house was one of those totally gutted by the fire.

Faipule Fagaima Larry Sanitoa explained that Tafuna’s Pulenu’u Liz Taliloa  assessed on Friday the family’s well-being, noting that she said “they are distraught, yet are in good emotional state.”

TEMCO was notified, and the Red Cross team visited the fire grounds to provide help, according to Ms Taliloa.

A call for help with donations of water, food, soap and clothing for the displaced families has gone out to the community. Essential basic needs listed are:

Clothing 

Shoes/slippers 

Water

Food (Canned goods, Rice, Flour, Sugar, noodles) 

Soap (hygiene products, baby wipes, washing detergent) 

Toothbrush /tooth paste 

Sleeping mats

blankets/bedsheets 

Towels

Toilet paper

Contacts for donations and deliveries are: Helen @782-3855 or Liz Taliloa - Tafuna Pulenuu 252-5897.

Helen Amituna’i is acting as the family’s representative. She and her husband with their 6 children are part of the 14 family members that were displaced.

Fagaima also pointed out that the donated clothes remaining from the Fagaima fire that were not needed could be sorted out for the family members in Ottovile.

The rash of fires currently happening on Tutuila have been the subject of concern in the community. To date, there have now been 10 fires since last year August. At least two of the fires are being investigated as arson, however there has been no official word exactly which fires these are.

Samoa News reported last week that Fagaima as chairman of the House Homeland Security Committee and a senior member of the House Public Safety Committee has requested reports on at least eight (8) of the fires reported since last year August from the Department of Search and Rescue (DSAR), of which the Fire Department is a part.

DSAR responded to the Tualauta faipule’s request, asking that Fagaima submit “a formal letter of request to the Office of the Governor for the fire investigation reports…”

item.title: Philippine Sailor Injured in Violent Clash with China Coast Guard off Second Thomas Shoal
item.description: MANILA, PHILIPPINES – A Philippine sailor was injured today at Second Thomas Shoal following a clash with a Chinese small boat at the contested South China Sea maritime feature. The melee resulted in a blow to the head of a Philippine service member, according to photos and video released from the incident by the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP). Previous injuries sustained by Filipino sailors, troops and civilians were inflicted by water cannon blasts, flying glass and a 2024 incident at Second Thomas Shoal which saw a Philippine Navy SEAL lose his thumb after his small boat was rammed.

item.title: As blazes spread near Paris, extreme heat is changing how France fights fires
item.description:
NÎMES, France — For almost two decades, French firefighting pilot Alexandre Jauffret’s routes were mostly contained to the hottest part of mainland France, the area around its southeastern coastline. He generally used his plane to scoop water from the Mediterranean Sea, or rivers and lakes nearby, and dump it on wildfires a short flight from the coast.

item.title: Tropical Gardening: Summer is mango and papaya season
item.description:
We usually think of lush tropical gardens when Hawaii comes to mind, but much of our land especially, on the leeward side, is quite dry. Figs, pomegranates, papaya and dates are just a few that come to mind, but mangoes are by far the most popular.

item.title: Am Samoa represented at inaugural Close Up NextGen Roundtable
item.description:
Amata congratulates Thessalonica Lagafuaina

Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Uifa’atali Aumua Amata is congratulating Thessalonica Lagafuaina for representing American Samoa at the inaugural Close Up NextGen Roundtable: Decision 2026 in Washington, D.C.

“Congratulations to Thessalonica for representing American Samoa in this important national forum and contributing our territory’s perspective alongside students from across the country,” said Congresswoman Amata. “I am proud of her willingness to learn, engage in thoughtful discussion, and represent our islands with distinction.”

Held July 8–11, the inaugural NextGen Roundtable brought together young people from across the nation and U.S. territories to examine major public policy issues, engage in respectful dialogue, and strengthen the skills of informed civic participation.

The program was hosted by the Close Up Foundation in partnership with the Stanford University Deliberative Democracy Lab, Generation Lab, and the Hoover Institution’s Center for Revitalizing American Institutions.

“This is the first year Close Up held the Next Gen Roundtable, and I was honored to represent our territory at this conference,” said Lagafuaina. “This is my second time representing American Samoa for the Close Up program.”

Lagafuaina previously represented American Samoa through the Close Up Foundation in 2025, when she and 13 other students traveled to Washington, D.C., for a two-week civic education program. During this year’s conference, she met students from across the United States and neighboring U.S. territories, reunited with mentors from her previous Close Up experience, and met Close Up President Mia Charity.

“Close Up is such a great opportunity, especially for our local kids, as it gives them the chance to see and meet other kids from around the nation and other islanders from nearby territories,” said Lagafuaina. “It also aids in developing an open mind, understanding more about the government, and getting a close up experience of so many historical monuments and places.”

Lagafuaina said the experience strengthened her understanding of government while creating friendships and connections that will last beyond the conference.

“Overall, I am grateful for the program and everything it had to offer; the lessons, skills, and many long term friendships,” said Lagafuaina.

“I appreciate Thessalonica’s commitment to representing American Samoa, and I encourage more of our students to pursue opportunities like Close Up that broaden their horizons, strengthen their leadership skills, and inspire future public service,” said Congresswoman Amata.

Lagafuaina is a recent graduate of Tafuna High School, Class of 2026, and is from the villages of Nuʻuuli and Futiga.

item.title: House requests reports on the eight fires that happened since August 2025
item.description:
By 
Samoa News staff
reporters@samoanews.com

Pago Pago, AMERICAN SAMOA — In a recent email to the director of Director of the Department of Search and Rescue (DSAR) Alefosio, Faipule Fagaima Larry Sanitoa requested reports on eight (8) fires that have occurred since August of last year in the territory.

Fagaima is the chairman of the House Homeland Security Committee and a senior member of the House Public Safety Committee.

On Tuesday, July 14th, the DSAR director responded to Fagaima’s request formally requesting that he submit “a formal letter of request to the Office of the Governor for the fire investigation reports.

“Once we receive authorization, we will promptly assist with your request,” he state.

Fagaima noted Alefosio’s response and copied the email to House Legal Counsel, Mr. Nathaniel Savali, and Legislative Financial Officer, Mr. Alfred Annadale. “They will submit a request for the fire investigation reports pursuant to ASCA 2.0602 (Cooperation of Government Agencies).”

In his email he states that they “are particularly interested in the cause of each fire, the actions taken to address these incidents, and the measures being taken to raise public awareness.

The Tualauta faipule continues, “Since the Legislature is in recess until Monday, July 27, we hope this provides sufficient time for you to prepare and submit these reports before our committee hearing.”

ORIGINAL REQUEST

Fagaima points out in his original request that the eight fires he identifies does not include “the recent fire last month at the RM Construction office near the TAOA office, which I understand the DPS CID division is currently investigating.”

The eight fires he is requesting information on are:

August 27, 2025 —        Fagatogo home

October 4, 2025 —        Pavaia’i home

April 13, 2026 —            Nu’uuli business (Pago Print Shop)

June 7, 2026 —             Pavaia’i home (Edwina)

June 18, 2026 —           Fagaima- four (4) homes

July 3, 2026 —               Fagatogo home

July 6, 2026 —               Fagatogo- DPS holding cells

July 12, 2026 —             Faleniu- 4 homes

The faipule states that while they “are grateful that there have been no serious injuries, these fires have caused significant hardship for many displaced families.”

He continues that “arson has been suspected in some of these cases, and I would like to know if active criminal investigations are underway.”

Fagaima goes on to address long-standing concerns in the community “regarding insufficient fire hydrants and low water pressure, particularly in the densely populated areas of the Tualauta district and Fagatogo village.”

ASPA management officials were copied in the same email, asking them for their input.

Additionally, the chairman of the House Public Safety Committee, Faipule Avagafono Maiava was copied, apprising him of his plan to request an urgent committee hearing to review DSAR’s reports and discuss the actions their office is taking to address and raise awareness about these issues.

The Criminal Intelligence & Investigative Bureau has since reached out to Fagaima to give him an update on an arson case it is investigating. The faipule has asked if CIIB is currently investigating any other arson cases.

BACKGROUND

Lack of funding to address fire fighting problems such as water pressure and inadequate fire hydrants to deliver the water has long been a problem in the territory. Lack of equipment and training for fire fighting personnel adds to the problems, with lack of real funding for a department that is often expected by then public to save lives and property in the community, with its “bare hands”.

Of note, the central fire station located in Fagatogo remains only partially operational, because it was formally closed more than a month ago by the Department of Health due to unsafe and unsanitary conditions. According to the DSAR director, two firefighters and the Fire Chief are still working out of an office inside the station, and that one fire truck remains housed there.

Fagatogo’s Faipule Malaeoletalu Melesio Gurr wrote to the Governor expressing concern that the closure of the Fagatogo Fire Station may have slowed response times, particularly during the fire behind the DPS & Fire station, with firefighters having to come from Tafuna to reach the scene.

Gurr also questioned why, after more than a month, the issues that led to the station’s closure — unsafe wiring, filthy bathrooms, and other hazards — have not yet been addressed.

The DSAR director acknowledged the delay in repairs, but pointed to renovations awaiting the processing of paperwork — which would include a construction or maintenance contract that would have to be bid out. There is no source of the funding for the contract mentioned.

Local News
Tags: 
house fires

item.title: Spanish Navy to Lead NATO’s Atlantic Task Force Until June 2027
item.description: The Spanish Navy has assumed command of NATO’s naval force dedicated to patrolling the North Atlantic and will lead the force for the next year, NATO announced Tuesday. From July of 2026 to June of 2027, NATO’s Commander Task Force Atlantic (CTF-AT) will be led by five Spanish ships, the Spanish Marine Corps landing force and eight ships from allied nations. Commander Task Force Atlantic operates under NATO Joint Force Command (JFC) Norfolk, which oversees NATO’s North Atlantic area of responsibility spanning the waters from the east coast of North America to Greenland, Iceland, the United Kingdom and Norway. CTF-AT

item.title: Another storm coming? NWS tracking tropical disturbance in Chuuk

item.title: Coast Guard Ends Middle East Mission, Moves Cutter Squadron to Western Pacific
item.description: The U.S. Coast Guard is transitioning its Patrol Forces Southwest Asia (PATFORSWA) to the Western Pacific, ending a more than 20-year forward-deployed mission in the Middle East. The Coast Guard’s Expeditionary Cutter Squadron that makes up PATFORSWA, which was previously forward deployed to Bahrain, will instead operate from Guam and the Pacific Islands, the service announced Wednesday. The transition from the Middle East to the Western Pacific is in response to national security requirements, reads the Coast Guard news release. “Coast Guard forces have always adapted to meet urgent national needs,” Adm. Kevin Lunday, Commandant of the Coast Guard, said

item.title: Saronic Announces Texas Site for New $3.2B Shipyard
item.description: Robot boat builder Saronic Technologies has tapped a site in Brownsville, Texas, for its ambitious Port Alpha $3.2 billion shipyard after securing a tax abatement deal from the local government. The 835-acre site in Cameron County is in the Port of Brownsville, home to the majority of the country’s shipbreaking industry. Speaking to reporters this week, Saronic CEO Dino Mavrookas said the greenfield site could employ up to 10,000 people over the next 10 years and would focus on both commercial and defense shipbuilding. Construction is set to begin this year. A facility is expected to be ready to build

item.title: Origins of the Jean P. Haydon Museum
item.description:
The American Samoa Council on Arts, Culture and Humanities has a special exhibition on display that focuses on American Samoa’s journey with the United States, called America 250.

It also re-introduces people to the origins of the Jean P. Haydon Museum — when gifts given to Gov. John Haydon and First Lady Jean in 1969 were first displayed on the 1st floor of the Governor’s mansion, and opened to the public for tours, on January 7, 1970.

The display was officially recognized by the Fono in 1971, as the ‘Museum of American Samoa’, and moved to the old naval commissary in 1973, after local funding plus a grant from the NEA made possible the acquisition and restoration of the building, where it is today.

The official opening ceremony for the museum was held on Flag Day, April 17, 1973. It was renamed the Jean P. Hayden Museum in 1974, when the Fono approved a referendum, at the end Gov. Haydon’s appointment.

[Courtesy photo]

item.title: Fono opening showcases noticeable conciliatory atmosphere
item.description:
By 
Asi Andrew Fa'asau
andrew@samoanews.com

Pago Pago, AMERICAN SAMOA — After the intense budget dispute in March — when the Fono accused the administration of violating budget law and moved to pursue legal action against the Pula and Pulu administration — a noticeably conciliatory atmosphere emerged between the Legislative and Executive Branches at Monday’s opening of the Fourth Regular Session of the 39th Legislature at the H. Rex Lee Auditorium.

In a departure from his past opening‑day addresses, Governor Pulaalii Nikolao Pula delivered his remarks almost entirely in English and used the moment to extend an olive branch to the Fono.

"Today however, I would like to begin this session by extending an olive branch," he began. "Though we may occasionally differ in our best to achieve our goals, we should never lose sight of the fact that our destination remains the same. Every decision we make should be guided by one simple question — Is this in the best interest of the people of American Samoa? If we remain committed to answering that question honestly, I am confident that we will continue making meaningful progress together.

Commenting on the government’s financial position, Governor Pulaali’i said his administration inherited mounting obligations that had accumulated over many years. Through what he described as hard work, a commitment to fiscal discipline, and difficult decision‑making, he asserted that the government has now reached a condition of financial stability.

Looking ahead, the governor noted that the Fiscal Year 2027 Budget will again reduce local revenues. Local revenue projections were lowered to $25 million in the FY 2026 Budget, and he said the further reduction planned for the new fiscal year will better align revenue estimates with actual collection capacity. He emphasized that the administration continues its efforts to grow the local economy, citing improvements in customs and tax systems, stronger revenue collection, and initiatives aimed at supporting the private sector.

Pulaali’i also highlighted the Territory’s partnership with the United States, pointing to federal support for the Levasa Google Cable and numerous infrastructure projects. He reported significant progress in the expenditure of ARPA funds, noting that of the $343 million awarded to American Samoa, more than $251 million has been spent in the past 18 months. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to completing the remaining 58 ARPA‑funded projects before the deadline at the end of this year.

The governor appealed to the Fono to pass forthcoming legislation concerning the American Samoa Government Employees Retirement Fund (ASGERF).

"This proposal is part of a broader strategy for the Territory's long-term financial position while protecting the retirement security of thousands of dedicated public servants," he explained. "Every retiree deserves confidence that the promises made to them will be honored. Every employee deserves confidence that the retirement system that they contribute to today will remain strong tomorrow. I respectfully and humbly ask for your thoughtful consideration of the submitted amendment bill as we work together to ensure its long-term sustainability."

He also highlighted several major infrastructure and economic development projects, including ongoing improvements at the airport and port. He said the $8.2 million airport parking lot is scheduled for completion next year, and construction of the new terminal is expected to begin in 2027. At the port, the government has secured funding to rehabilitate the main dock, with bidding for a significant portion of the project set to begin next month.

Turning to transportation services for Manu‘a, Governor Pulaali’i stressed that the islands cannot rely solely on the Manu‘atele. He referenced the vessel’s recent grounding due to deficiencies cited by the U.S. Coast Guard and noted that the Manu‘atele requires roughly half a million dollars annually for proper maintenance. He said the government is actively seeking a stable funding source to ensure reliable service for Manu‘a residents.

Responding on behalf of the Senate, President Tuaolo Manaia Fruean began with a verse from a Samoan song about forgiveness and setting aside past offenses — a gesture that set a reflective tone for his remarks. As chair of the ASGERF Board of Trustees, Tuaolo reminded the Fono that the government still carries an estimated $20 million obligation to the Retirement Fund. He argued that the current 14‑percent employer contribution rate is unsustainable and said he hopes lawmakers will identify a workable path forward during this session.

The administration has proposed lowering the employer contribution to 8 percent. Tuaolo referenced what he described as a Russian proverb — “Your enemy is a yes‑man, but your friend always argues with you” — and assured the governor that “the Fono is your friend”. He encouraged the governor to actively seek guidance from both senators and representatives (faipule).

Tuaolo closed by recalling advice once given to him and the House Speaker by the late Governor Lolo Moliga: that a new administration benefits from steady counsel, and that the Fono’s leadership should help guide the Pula and Pulu team as it finds its footing.

He reported significant progress in the expenditure of ARPA funds, noting that of the $343 million awarded to American Samoa, more than $251 million has been spent in the past 18 months. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to completing the remaining 58 ARPA‑funded projects before the deadline at the end of this year.
The governor appealed to the Fono to pass forthcoming legislation concerning the American Samoa Government Employees Retirement Fund (ASGERF).
"This proposal is part of a broader strategy for the Territory's long-term financial position while protecting the retirement security of thousands of dedicated public servants," he explained. "Every retiree deserves confidence that the promises made to them will be honored. Every employee deserves confidence that the retirement system that they contribute to today will remain strong tomorrow. I respectfully and humbly ask for your thoughtful consideration of the submitted amendment bill as we work together to ensure its long-term sustainability."
He also highlighted several major infrastructure and economic development projects, including ongoing improvements at the airport and port. He said the $8.2 million airport parking lot is scheduled for completion next year, and construction of the new terminal is expected to begin in 2027. At the port, the government has secured funding to rehabilitate the main dock, with bidding for a significant portion of the project set to begin next month.
Turning to transportation services for Manu‘a, Governor Pulaali’i stressed that the islands cannot rely solely on the Manu‘atele. He referenced the vessel’s recent grounding due to deficiencies cited by the U.S. Coast Guard and noted that the Manu‘atele requires roughly half a million dollars annually for proper maintenance. He said the government is actively seeking a stable funding source to ensure reliable service for Manu‘a residents.
Responding on behalf of the Senate, President Tuaolo Manaia Fruean began with a verse from a Samoan song about forgiveness and setting aside past offenses — a gesture that set a reflective tone for his remarks. As chair of the ASGERF Board of Trustees, Tuaolo reminded the Fono that the government still carries an estimated $20 million obligation to the Retirement Fund. He argued that the current 14‑percent employer contribution rate is unsustainable and said he hopes lawmakers will identify a workable path forward during this session.
The administration has proposed lowering the employer contribution to 8 percent. Tuaolo referenced what he described as a Russian proverb — “Your enemy is a yes‑man, but your friend always argues with you” — and assured the governor that “the Fono is your friend”. He encouraged the governor to actively seek guidance from both senators and representatives (faipule).
Tuaolo closed by recalling advice once given to him and the House Speaker by the late Governor Lolo Moliga: that a new administration benefits from steady counsel, and that the Fono’s leadership should help guide the Pula and Pulu team as it finds its footing.

item.description:
